newsitem.title: GERMANY: China tensions cost Siemens no contracts.
newsitem.headline: China tensions cost Siemens no contracts.

text.p: German electronics giant Siemens AG says it lost no major contracts in China due to increased tensions with Germany, but that it was glad the situation was now resolved.

"I am very glad" Foreign Ministers Klaus Kinkel and Qian Qichen had been able to iron out their differences, said Guenter Wilhelm, Siemens board member in charge of Asia/Pacific business. "We were trembling."
Beijing on Tuesday reinstated an invitation to Kinkel that it withdrew in June after the German parliament passed a resolution accusing China of trying to eradicate Tibet's cultural identity.
Siemens chairman Heinrich von Pierer, who is also head of the Asia-Pacific Committee of German Business, expressed sentiments similar to Wilhelm's on Tuesady.

Wilhelm told reporters he knew of two major German enterprises that had lost major contracts due to the heightened tensions, which were also a "gigantic problem" for Siemens even if it lost no business.
Companies like Siemens are "extraordinarily dependent" on political currents, he said.
Siemens expects its orders in China to total 1.8 billion marks in the current business year, which ends September 30. Its 35 subsidiaries and affiliates there employ 8,500 workers.
About 40,000 of Siemens 210,000 domestic jobs stem from Asian business. This figure should hold steady for the next five years even as Asian local content increases, Wilhelm said.
Asian sales now total about 10 billion marks, 30 percent of which represents local content. That ratio could rise to 40 or 50 percent in five years.
Wilhelm repeated his earlier forecast that Asia/Pacific incoming orders could rise to 25 billion marks by 2000 from 15 billion in 1995/96.
Sales may rise to 21 to 22 billion marks, he said. Siemens plans to invest three to four billion marks in the region over the next five years, and its workforce may rise to 70,000 from 45,000
